html:
Kobildzan: From Survivors in a Hole to Dragons in Their Own Right

Survey-region classification: Wescann / Gerudia.

Flag

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 68/100 | Autocracy 74/100 | Magic–Artifice 10/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 100/100) | Pluralism 70/100. The v2.1 values rating is Neutral (62/100), with a mixed trajectory. Unifying the three scales, creating a homeland for a persecuted people, a multi-ethnic technocracy, and post-disaster reconstruction are substantial positive evidence; bodily alteration and the continental catastrophe caused by the Dragon's Roar weigh against dignity and restraint. The catastrophe is assessed by intent, foreseeability, avoidability, victims' perspectives, and subsequent conduct; casualty scale alone does not make it a deliberate annihilation.

First survive the siege of stronger neighbours through traps and attrition; then unite the three scales, rebuild the Dragon Coast, and use artificery to remake flesh—until “worshipping dragons” becomes “becoming dragons.”

Story: Very high | Mission-tree length: Extremely long (13 direct shared prologue missions among the predecessors; 49 direct missions after formation) | Mission-tree update: Local files current through 2026-09-07 | Distinctiveness: Exceptional | Tedium: Extreme | Early pressure: Extreme | Expansion: Upper-moderate

Identity and History

Kobildzan (Z38) is not a 1444 starting country. It forms after Redscale (A26), Bluescale (A27), or Greenscale (A28) unifies the Dragon Coast. All three are kobold states that follow the Kobold Dragon Cult, but they have long fought one another: Redscale prizes courage, Bluescale preserves knowledge of dragons and ancestors, and Greenscale is known for the resilience needed to survive isolation and encirclement.【Local history / mission text】

The offline English Wiki traces their shared earlier history to the Dragonwake: the blue dragon Tayekan brought Dragon Coast kobolds, originally living underground, to the surface; a kobold uprising destroyed the first Gnomish Hierarchy; and the community then split into Red, Blue, and Green scales. They fought one another while also facing Gnomish remnants and powerful Cannorian neighbours, and were gradually pushed back into the Dragonspine Mountains.【Wiki】 In 1444, the three scales remain separate. The current English country-history files name their rulers Levaz Sozax (Redscale), Tayekar Crozamor (Bluescale), and Dervaszix Korlak (Greenscale). Kobildzan's own history file defines the formed-country state; it must not be misrepresented as a kingdom already present at the campaign's start.【Local history script】

Campaign Story and Main Arc

The first act is not world conquest but avoiding extinction. The three scales are caught between the Gnomes, Gawed, Lorent, and other powerful neighbours. Militarily and institutionally outmatched, they must turn terrain, forts, and kobold traps into weapons. Traps trade manpower and construction costs for defensive strength, attrition, and trade benefits; if a fort falls, the defensive system may collapse with it.【Local script】 The player must first absorb rival clans, defeat Nimscodd, and hold the Dragon Coast before Kobildzan can be formed.

After formation, the mission tree reinterprets the strengths of the three scales as a shared identity: Redscale courage, Bluescale wisdom, and Greenscale resilience become three legacies of one people rather than mutually exclusive bloodline labels. The “Purple Union” first reconciles the Red and Blue scales; the country then teaches the next generation their common history and turns kobolds from clans hiding to survive into a people able to govern the Dragon Coast.【Local mission text】

The second act is revival. The player refines traps and coastal trade goods, accumulates dragon hoards, restores dragon festivals, and develops the many aspects of the Dragon Cult. At the same time, the country develops artificery, joining religious devotion to technological experimentation. Missions send the player to Aelantir, the Haraf colonial region, and other lands in search of dragons of different colours, on a global “Dragon Hunt,” upgrading the faith's aspects and establishing contact with actual dragons.【Local script / official development diary】 The source names a further destination whose English form could not be confirmed in the representative current-Mod localisation checked for this translation. Kobildzan is therefore both a defensive minor power and a country of colonisation, long voyages, and global exploration.

The third act pushes that ambition to a dangerous extreme. Artificers and dragon priests develop the bespoke “Dragon Ascension” invention, using bodily alteration to give kobolds the bodies and abilities of dragons. The state moves further toward technocracy and chooses between empowering a small elite and making the transformation available to a broader population.【Local script】 Its most affecting dimension is that a people long despised and hunted can finally define itself. Its most troubling is the assumption that its own ascension is a universal answer—and the possibility that it will decide for others what bodies and civilisations count as progress.

The Dragon's Roar: A Second Struggle to Survive After Victory

Kobildzan's sharpest turn is not its final triumph but the catastrophe. After the “Kobildzan Celebration,” the earth shakes and the sky darkens, triggering the “Dragon's Roar”: mountains split, lava and ash sweep across Cannor, dragon hoards are destroyed, and the Dragon Coast and broad surrounding areas suffer devastation of 20 to 100 severity. Kobildzan itself also loses a large amount of development.【Local event script】

This is not a tragedy confined to flavour text: it can genuinely destroy years of the player's development in the middle or late game. The country must rescue survivors amid the ash, rebuild, preserve the memory of the dead, and reconsider its faith in dragons. The later route neither simply rejects the Dragon Cult nor treats the catastrophe as a miracle without cost. It asks kobolds to acknowledge the price of pursuing divinity and to seek a revival that does not keep wasting the world. In the end, the player gathers dragon representatives from different cultures, restores ties among dragons, and attempts to bring back the “Age of Dragons.”【Local mission and event text】

Core Mechanics

  1. Kobold traps and attritional defence: Build and upgrade traps in designated provinces, using fort defence, enemy attrition, and terrain to wear down invaders far stronger than you. This is not a peripheral bonus: it is the opening survival loop.
  2. Unifying the three scales: Redscale, Bluescale, and Greenscale share 13 direct prologue missions; after forming Z38, the campaign continues into 49 direct missions. Do not add these into 62 “unique missions”: the prologue is shared by the three starting countries.
  3. Dragon Cult aspects and the global Dragon Hunt: Accumulate hoards, hold celebrations, unlock and strengthen the aspects associated with different dragon colours, and then travel across continents in search of real dragons. Religion, exploration, and national narrative share one progression arc.
  4. Artificery and Dragon Ascension: Bespoke inventions evolve with mission progress. Technocracy, artificer factions, and bodily alteration jointly determine who can “become a dragon,” making this the entry's most distinctive build system.
  5. Revival, destruction, and revival again: Rebuild the Dragon Coast, experience the continent-scale devastation of the Dragon's Roar, and recover from the ruins. The mid-to-late game therefore brings real resource pressure and a major narrative turn.

Phased Play

At the start, prioritise military technology, traps, and key mountain passes. Redscale usually has a more direct early-war opening; Bluescale is better positioned to defend the northern routes; Greenscale emphasises survival in isolation. All three can form Kobildzan. The choice mainly changes the prologue perspective and opening tempo, not the main post-formation tree.【Local script; community strategy is only a report of player experience】

After forming the country, manage domestic integration, coastal development, religious festivals, artificery, and colonial exploration at the same time. The middle game is not simply wide expansion: you need mission regions and global footholds, but also hoards, traps, the capital, and a technological base. The late game turns to intercontinental dragon-hunting and bodily alteration, before the Dragon's Roar and large-scale reconstruction. A full campaign commonly runs from 1444 well into the late-game dates.

The characteristic loop is: use traps to survive stronger enemies → unite the three scales and reclaim the coast → build hoards and an artificer state → seek dragons across continents → advance Dragon Ascension → endure the Dragon's Roar → rebuild the ruins and reunite the dragons.

Legacy EOIV Personality and Moral Assessment (Not the Current Production Scores)

Legacy EOIV profile: The source-era assessment says Kobildzan must expand beyond the Dragon Coast and establish global footholds, so it leans toward expansion. It describes technocracy, cultural unification, and state-directed transformation as strongly order-oriented; combining religion, artificery, and biological alteration as one of the dataset's most radical innovation paths; and “making kobolds dragons and reuniting the dragons” as an overwhelmingly vision-driven ambition. This is retained as historical source content, not substituted for the current v2.1 personality coordinates above.

The legacy assessment gives a moral result of Neutral (42/100, medium confidence). Its positive evidence includes ending the civil wars among the three scales, creating a common homeland for a persecuted people, later bringing gnomes, goblins, and Ruinborn Elves into its artificer civilisation, and accepting responsibility for reconstruction after the disaster. Its negative rationale lists wars of expansion, technocratic concentration of authority over bodily alteration, painful and potentially coercive fleshcraft, and a continent-scale disaster caused by a state religious project. These are the inherited assessment's reasons, not a new v2.1 judgment; this paragraph does not endorse war alone as negative evidence. The source describes Kobildzan as neither an evil country whose purpose is cruelty nor a harmless utopia, and says institutional choices can shift how it plays out.

The source article contains both the current v2.1 opening result and this inherited legacy EOIV profile. Both are retained and clearly distinguished; the legacy result is not the current production score, and neither source conclusion has been silently recalculated or reconciled.

Who Should Play It—and Who Shouldn't

Recommended for players who enjoy extremely difficult openings, mountain defence, dense mechanics, colonial exploration, artificery, and long-form narrative. Its greatest reward is not mere numerical power growth, but following a frightened people from underground through unification, revival, hubris, catastrophe, and reflection, until they can speak to dragons as equals.

Avoid it if you cannot tolerate likely restarts, an opening that depends on attrition to exhaust stronger enemies, simultaneous colonial and domestic management, or a mid-to-late-game story event that actively destroys a great deal of development. Players who have completed the campaign often praise its story and late-game artificer strength, while also mentioning repeated early attempts, numerous competing objectives, and late-game performance pressure. Those are player experiences, not guaranteed results in the current version.

Evidence Boundaries

Current identity, formation relationships, mission counts, traps, Dragon Ascension, and the Dragon's Roar are grounded in local v1.37.5.0 scripts and localisation. The offline Wiki's Kobildzan country page is a stub; the main historical supplements came from the English Kobold and Kobold Dragon Cult entries. Official Reddit material records the 2024 rework's design and release context. Two player posts support only reported experiences such as common Redscale openings, a long and difficult early campaign, strong late-game play, and an appreciated story; they do not establish current numerical mechanics.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Kobildzan (Z38) — Kobildzani Ideas

Set ID: Z38_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = Z38
    }

Kobildzani Traditions

  • Hostile Attrition: +200% (hostile_attrition; raw value 2).

  • Fort maintenance: -15% (fort_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.15).

1. Equality Under Kobildzan Act

While the formation of Kobildzan had brought unification to kobolds, they still had petty squabbles internally. Eventually, this gave cause for the creation of the Treaty of Kobildzan, which indicated 'no kobold was to loot another kobold', which was later extrapolated to Equality Under Kobildzan Act which proclaimed that all kobolds are equal, regardless of scale colour.

  • Stability cost modifier: -15% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.15).

2. Dragonheight Undercities

By the Age of Unraveling much of koboldkind had been pushed back to the deepest depths of the Dragonheight Mountains. However, with their newfound knowledge of the surface and the burgeoning field of artificery, the kobold race boomed and expanded their natural caverns into their own crude mimicry of the underground dwarven cities of old.

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.1).

3. Centralize the Dragon Cult

The worship of dragons in kobold society was extremely loose throughout the majority of history and had no actual grounds of legitimacy. After the formation of Kobildzan, the worship of dragons came under control of the state, which led the creation of actual religious texts, and reforms such as documented dragon heritage and the tales of significant dragons becoming established literature.

  • True faith tolerance: +1 (tolerance_own; raw value 1.0).

4. Kobildzani Fire & Swarm

Kobolds are an impatient lot - and that does not bold well with the line infantry of conventional warfare. Kobolds saw the opportunity with numbers and their ingenuity in firearms: masses of kobolds would fire at will against the enemy whilst an even greater horde would swarm the enemy with traditional melee weapons.

  • Movement speed: +7.5% (movement_speed; raw value 0.075).

  • Infantry combat ability: +5% (infantry_power; raw value 0.05).

5. Hoard Tax

Part religious tithe, part contributions to the state. The Hoard Tax was introduced in 1670 to formalize each kobold's contribution to the Dragon Cult (which had then turned into another office of the country).

  • National tax modifier: +10% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.1).

6. Kobold Junk Ships

Historically the survival of the gnomish peoples on islands like Nimscodd was due to the fact that kobolds loathed water and never had a proper navy... until now. Under the command of junkyard owner Sheezax Lexxa, Kobildzan commissioned its first navy in 1734 which was all made of metal junk. The very same navy ended up circumnavigating the entire world in 1747.

  • Naval maintenance modifier: -10% (naval_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.1).

7. Kobold School of Artificery

The gnomes love to tinker and make everything ingeniously perfect. The dwarves love efficiency and a well-oiled machine. What do kobolds love? Explosions - and lots of them!

  • Artillery combat ability: +10% (artillery_power; raw value 0.10).

  • Land fire damage: +10% (fire_damage; raw value 0.1).

Kobildzani Ambition

  • Regiment recruitment time: -50% (global_regiment_recruit_speed; raw value -0.5).

Redscale (A26) — Redscale Ideas

Set ID: A26_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A26 # Redscale
    }

Redscale Traditions

  • global_manpower_modifier：+10% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Manpower recovery speed: +15% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.15).

1. Scavengers Reign

Before the Dragonwake, kobold civilization thrived off of tightly-wound corridors, lava-based metallurgy, and cavern-dwelling fungi. On the surface, however, kobolds could rely on nothing familiar. They had to learn to utilize surface foods, metals, and tactics; and they had to do so all while the weight of the world bore down upon them. The proto-Redscales scavenged everything they could from their surroundings, surviving through innovative grit.

Only one practice constantly eluded the coastal kobolds, shipmaking. This wasn’t for a lack of trying. Nimscodd sank whatever kobold raft and cog they could find, making naval development nigh-impossible. Ever since, the Redscales have scavenged every shipwreck they could find, building a makeshift fleet to hold off the tide. Uho ‘the Raftmaker’ was the leading expert of this new wave of kobold shipbuilding, notoriously having been sunk tenfold by the patrolling gnomes and yet surviving to build more ships.

  • Ship Cost: -5% (global_ship_cost; raw value -0.05).

  • Technology cost: -2% (technology_cost; raw value -0.02).

2. Trapherders

While learning the ways of the surface proved challenging, the greatest difficulties the kobolds met in those initial years on the surface was how the familiar became unfamiliar. Herding had long been a staple of kobold culture, an easy task given the cramped nature of the caverns. On the surface, though, managing the open fields seemed an insurmountable task.

The Redscales, however, were able to use their trapping skills to their advantage; the livestock could roam all they wanted if they had nowhere to go when it was time to get harvested. They created an extensive trapping system which can now be found across the Dragon Coast, constantly utilizing it to keep the herds in check. Soon, the lands of the Redscales became known for having plentiful meat and wool, and so the tribe became known for its woolen amenities, such as bedding and other assortment of covers to keep their supplies dry and the wind off of them.

  • Production efficiency: +10% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

3. Make Them Fear the Red

Many battles were fought over dominion of the Dragon Coast, and especially over the Dragondowns, during the Little Wars, but the Battle of Besurzalay gave such notoriety to a warband of scarlet-hued kobolds that it earned them the name ‘Redscales’. Besurzalay, a port town that had formerly been known as 'Downfield', marked the point where the Kobold tribes began to take the shape they have become known for; the Kobold commander, Vren Scarlethue, coated his army’s scales with scarlet war-paint and taunted the Reverians that had landed upon the shores to attempt to pillage the town. The human invaders let their guard down, assuming the monstrous kobolds weren’t capable of rationality, given their strategic choice to stand-out in red, which led them to naively step onto spiked pitfalls that had been set up before the battle. After that, the conflict turned into a rout and the Reverians that managed to flee back into their ships told stories to the rest of Cannor about the fearsome Redscale Kobolds.

  • Morale damage: +10% (morale_damage; raw value 0.1).

4. Born Through Cunning

Said to bear the blood of Nimrith the Red himself, the legendary Redscale ruler Aakax Sozax did not begin with the respect of his fellows. Initially, Aakax was little more than a pariah, shunned for claiming that it was a dragon’s cunning rather than its strength that made them great, heresy for the clan that prided itself on its ferocity. Then the gnomes attacked. The old chief did traditional Redscale tactics and was obliterated. Despite being a fodder soldier, Aakax convinced some kobolds to break away with him. They then tricked the gnome commander into retreating by making them think that another kobold army was coming in. Hailed a hero, Aakax was made the new chief, heralding a new era prioritizing cunning over tradition.

  • Reform progress growth: +15% (reform_progress_growth; raw value 0.15).

5. Colour Competition

The kobolds of the Dragon Coast take pride in the colours of their scales, seeing it as a mark of their draconic heritage to be such vibrant monochromatic beings like the great wyrms themselves. Competition between the three kinsfolk are fierce, with it being seen as the great challenge to make your mark in history by upholding the greatness of your scale-trivu’s legend.

  • Innovativeness gain: +0.25 (innovativeness_gain; raw value 0.25).

  • Promote culture cost: -12.5% (promote_culture_cost; raw value -0.125).

6. Tayekans Wake

It was a dark and stormy night when Tayekan flew, lightning crackled as the storm howled and the Dragondepths were blown open and blasted by the elements from within. Tayekan had transformed from a kobold guise to true draconic majesty. Yet wrothful as his escape was; it was a numinous experience to know that a dragon had lived among them, they, the kobolds who had been trapped within the depths specifically all this time.

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

7. On Malliaths Bones

The shape of the Coast that gives the region its name was something the Kobolds took to be evident proof of their claim to the bones and remains of the great dragon Malliath, said to have been slain by the Cannorian Gods. The land is seen as venerable ground, fit only for the most devoted to the dragons to walk upon and so even in their disorganised state they have fought tenaciously for each rock and pass as Gnomes, Reavers and more besides lay covetous claim upon their home.

  • Fort defense: +15% (defensiveness; raw value 0.15).

Redscale Ambitions

  • Regiment recruitment time: -33% (global_regiment_recruit_speed; raw value -0.33).

Bluescale (A27) — Bluescale Ideas

Set ID: A27_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

Bluescale Traditions

  • global_manpower_modifier：+10% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Manpower recovery speed: +15% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.15).

1. Trust in Traps, Not the Other

In the mid 1400s, Buruzagi Tayekar Crozamor of the Bluescales received a message from the Redscales requesting a treaty of mutual defense. Buruzagi’s response was as follows:

“It makes perfect sense that you would come to me for help, that you would seek an alliance. All know that no matter how many times the Bluescales are attacked, our tunnels shall never be breached. But you, who live in fields and shallow hills, are vulnerable; if a single Red trap is broken, there is nowhere for you to hide. And so, you want help. More bodies to die for your shoddy defenses.

There will be no alliance. If the gnomes, of all groups, cause you to seek aid, then your viraxia is nothing more than a hatchling unable to even dig a simple hole. Maybe, once you’ve learned what your claws are for, I'll lend your tribe mine."

  • Land morale recovery speed: +10% (recover_army_morale_speed; raw value 0.1).

2. Tayekan's Takers

One day, Tayekan met two kobolds. Tayekan asked these kobolds for somewhere to sleep. The pair were shocked, and said he was far too large to fit in any cavern or cave. This, though, was a lie; the pair had found the largest cavern in the area, but didn’t want to share.

Tayekan was annoyed, but not angry. He asked for a bed of gems and gold, for it was the only thing he could sleep on. Again, the young kobolds lied. Despite having found incredible wealth, they said that even if every kobold worked together, they could barely pile enough to give half of Tayekan a comfortable sleep!

Tayekan, sensing their lies, turned to the kobolds. “You lied,” he said. “Thus, until this cavern is full of enough wealth for me to swim in, you will never see me again.” With that, Tayekan flew through the caverns out into the sky, scattering the kobolds’ treasure across the world. The commotion brought the rest of the kobolds to the cavern, and the two kobolds explained what happened. One was so angry at losing Tayekan he had turned red. The other was so sick from their actions, he turned green. And so it fell to us Bluescales to hunt down the kobolds’ hoards, to bring Tayekan back.

  • Looting speed: +50% (loot_amount; raw value 0.5).

3. Mushroom Masters

"The Cannorians wait for miracles, using veiled half-truths to justify belief. The gnomes ignore any evidence of divinity, concocting any flimsy sophistry to use as evidence for their 'Thought'. But Malliath provides directly to his children.

Look at the dragonfire flamepuff. Malliath donates his very flames to us, allowing the fire breathing of gods to be utilised by the common kobold. It is no coincidence this firey red fungus grows in the dragon coast- it's clearly a gift from the world serpent himself.

Gaze upon the miner's delight. Malliath's heart aches as he watches his children toil in the caverns. He yearns to give us a respite. And so he does. A fungus that eats only rock, leaving perfectly shaped caverns for our use. A true miracle of mycelium every week.

Feast your eyes and stomachs upon the scalespores. The biggest danger in the mines is not a cave-in, it's starvation. And so Malliath gave salvation unto his children with a mushroom that can grow on their very bodies. Its itch is a reminder to eat, and its taste a tool to ward off gluttony." - Manuscripts of Wrek Cyanscale

  • Army attrition: -15% (land_attrition; raw value -0.15).

4. Legacy of the First Viraxia

The Bluescales were not the first "Viraxia," or "Hierarchy," of the Dragon Coast kobolds: but they were the first that survived for longer than a generation. Unlike the other attempted Viraxias– like the Maroonscales of 870, or the Mosscales of 906– the Bluescales were primarily formed out of a diplomatic union.

Months were spent in meetings, ensuring that while one kobold would rule over all others, each tribe would retain autonomy, and their leaders would have direct access to the monarch. Most importantly, the 'Buruzagi' would choose an heir from one of the other trivuak of the Bluescales, adopting them as their own child. When the first Buruzagi died, everyone braced for collapse... but the new Buruzagi took power, and the state was maintained.

  • Advisor cost: -10% (advisor_cost; raw value -0.1).

The kobolds of the Dragon Coast take pride in the colours of their scales, seeing it as a mark of their draconic heritage to be such vibrant monochromatic beings like the great wyrms themselves. Competition between the three kinsfolk are fierce, with it being seen as the great challenge to make your mark in history by upholding the greatness of your scale-trivu’s legend.

  • Promote culture cost: -12.5% (promote_culture_cost; raw value -0.125).

Greenscale (A28) — Greenscale Ideas

Set ID: A28_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = A28 #Greenscale
    }

Greenscale Traditions

  • global_manpower_modifier：+10% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Manpower recovery speed: +15% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.15).

1. Children of the Storm

“Land, skies, and sea. The land was given to us by Malliath, whose bones hold up the world. We are Malliath's children, and we must care for our ancient father. Waste nothing of the land, so that his gifts won’t be in vain. Every crag and cliff, every pit and cavern, was made for us. We need only build on what we were given, to keep ourselves safe. The skies were given to us by Tayekan, whose storm and wrath propelled us farther than our other-scaled kin dared go. We are Tayekan's children, and we should cherish his gift. Though he has abandoned us, the sky remains. Cherish the fleeting blue, and wield the storms against our foes. We need only understand what we were given, to keep ourselves free. The sea remains aloof, given to us by a stranger. We are that stranger's children, and we must find them. The sea is mysterious, its currents give and take life. Learn its ways, its ebbs and flows, so that it too may shield us. We need only discover what we were given, so that we may begin to give back."

  • Transcribed Greenscale Oral Tradition

  • Stability cost modifier: -15% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.15).

2. Quiet Neighbor

"By that time, hours had passed, and I'd all but given up calling for help. Treading a mix of saltwater, piss, and sweat, at the bottom of a pit trap... You wonder how much glory is really worth. They don't write songs about the ones who die like this. I'd already tossed my shield, armor, anything that could weigh me down. I think... I think that was what saved me. When I saw the makeshift hatch move, saw that green little face poking in, I thought they were going to kill me. I think they thought so, too; they had a spear ready and pointed. But when they saw me– soggy, unarmored, unarmed– they paused. I heard them speaking their strange squawking language, and then they lowered down a rope. I don't know why they spared me. They never said, I never asked. They led me at spear point to the border and just... let me go. It was a completely silent march, save for the very end when one of them spoke: ‘Leave us to our quiet,’ they said. And I think we should."

  • Account of Marlen the Broken, sole survivor of the Fouler's Fifty mercenary band.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

3. Finding the Dragons

"At the time of its writing, I thought my report regarding the Greenscales adequate. I did not yet understand how quickly things move in this new land. Now, conscience compels me to admit that I had... omitted certain details. It is true, I was captured in a cunning snare trap whilst mapping the territory around our new homeland of Celmaldor. And it is true that I was questioned by a kobold who called herself ‘Itla Humanspeaker,’ and that I revealed nothing I thought might pose a risk to our people. And my recommendation that their borders be respected and left alone stands. Yet as I think back on my encounter, I feel unease in regards to one question. "Thisss... All... Ale...
